tag: the key screen goes back to counting only pages
why: L1, and it is the defect FU-348 was filed for. A key whose consumer is a ROUND is surfaced by the CLI that prints it, so counting only pages made such a key reach 'no surface' BY CONSTRUCTION — and FU-345's whole subject was that the round-start step states its own width, which it does by printing it. The mutation keeps the variable and the branch, so nothing reads as missing.

tag: a mere mention counts as a surface, which W493 already paid to narrow once
new:
aliases = _aliases_of(c, key)
        for seg in [Path(c).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")]:
why: L2. Treating the WHOLE FILE as one emitting segment is exactly the narrowing the W493 refutation already reversed: 'skip if ANY other file mentions it' made the printed label false, because this process requires a register row and habitually writes a source-substring guard in the same commit. A name that is assigned, imported or asserted but never EMITTED is not a surface.

tag: the word print in a comment or a string is read as a call
old:
emits = (isinstance(f, ast.Name) and f.id == "print") or (
            isinstance(f, ast.Attribute) and f.attr in _LOG_METHODS)
        if not emits:
            continue
why: L3. Counting EVERY call as emitting is the textual-proxy failure in its purest form: a key passed to any function at all would read as surfaced. The leg drives a synthetic file where `print` appears in a comment and inside a string literal, and where a key is read and merely RETURNED — none of which puts a value in front of anyone.

tag: an unparseable file is read as having emitting calls
why: L3. A screen cannot claim a surface it could not read. Falling back to the raw text on a parse failure is the worst available behaviour: the files most likely to fail to parse are the ones a round is halfway through editing, so the screen would clear keys precisely when the tree is least trustworthy.

tag: two levels of indirection are followed, so the screen reaches further than it claims
why: L4, and the point is not that two levels would be WRONG — it is that the helper documents ONE. A screen quietly reaching further than it says is this family's own defect: a later round reading the docstring would form a false picture of what was checked. If two levels are ever wanted, the docstring changes with the code.

tag: a one-character alias is trusted, so almost any emitting call becomes a surface
old: return {a for a in out if len(a) >= 2}
why: L4. A single-letter binding would match a word boundary in nearly any print statement in the file, so the screen would CLEAR keys it had not seen surfaced. A false surface is worse than a missed one here for exactly that reason — the miss leaves a lead, the false clear removes one.

tag: no-page and no-surface-at-all become one message again
old:
reaches NO SURFACE AT ALL - no "
                           f"page renders it and no print or log statement emits it - {where}"
why: L5, and the row's closing line names it: 'Until then a round must read the lead as no PAGE, not nobody.' One message for two states meant a round could not tell a key shown only on a CLI from a key shown nowhere — and the first needs no action while the second is the finding.

tag: the check's label says 'no surface' while it checks pages and printed lines
old: "keys": ("a key produced but shown by neither a page nor a printed line", check_keys),
new: "keys": ("a key produced but read by no surface", check_keys),
why: L5. The old label was FALSE about the very key this row was filed for: the key had a surface, and the label said it had none. A label is the first thing a round reads and the last thing anyone checks, which is why it is guarded rather than left to care.

tag: the module stops recording why this is structural rather than textual
old: that its own screen family has produced four precision defects with one shape — "a textual proxy
new: that this is a convenient place to look — ("a convenient proxy
why: L5. Four precision defects in one screen family all had the same shape, and the only thing stopping a fifth is that the reason is written where the next round will read it. A fix whose rationale is lost becomes a fix someone simplifies.
